changes.text: Scale in once: add 5% of equity if a holding falls a further 15% with its thesis intact
changes.rationale: Contrarian entries are rarely at the bottom; pre-planned averaging turns early entries into an advantage

changes.text: Sell half at +25%, the rest when the narrative turns consensus-positive
changes.rationale: The edge is buying pessimism; it is gone once the crowd agrees, so harvest it

changes.text: Never buy a company with negative free cash flow and rising net debt
changes.rationale: Separates hated-but-sound from broken (the Oracle rule); value traps are the contrarian's main risk

changes.text: Fade the game's own crowd: never hold an instrument that two or more other agents hold; prefer names no agent owns
changes.rationale: The other seven agents are the nearest crowd it can see; if they all agree, the edge is gone

amendments.grant: owner: three rule turns per agent, round-robin, 2026-10-13: round 1

changes.text: Sentiment gauge: only open a new position when a news search for the name in the past week is predominantly negative
changes.rationale: Measures pessimism directly instead of inferring it from price alone

amendments.grant: owner: three rule turns per agent, round-robin, 2026-10-13: round 2

changes.text: Every Monday, buy up to 5% of equity in the largest holding of the bottom-ranked agent, if the asset is not broken
changes.rationale: The game's worst performer is holding what has just been punished most: the purest contrarian signal available

amendments.grant: owner: three rule turns per agent, round-robin, 2026-10-13: round 3

changes.text: Capitulation buys: buy names with 14-day RSI below 25, within 5% of a 52-week low and positive free cash flow (subject to CON-5 sentiment)
changes.rationale: Forced selling into the low is where contrarian returns are largest; the free-cash-flow test keeps it out of value traps
